class_guess: defect-list counter: left-end carry transducer + eat phase over a 1010 background (multi-level, no template)
summary: 1010 tape with 00/11 defects; a carry transducer and an eat rule cover 99.3% of bounces; the macro level is open.
mechanism: The tape is 1010... with isolated extra symbols (00 = extra 0, 11 = extra 1), and every sweep complements what it crosses. So the state is a list (10)^n0 x1 (10)^n1 ... of segment lengths n_i and extra bits x_i. It halts iff it reaches 1 1 0 <C (window W5 with 11 directly left of 00).

Two exact rules cover 99.3% of record moves to 1e10. L (31%) is a left-end bounce acting as a 4-state carry transducer on (n_i mod 2, x_{i+1}), with deltas 0, +-1, +2, +3, +4 (30,720/30,720 real, 900/900 random). E (68%) is a 000 marker eating the segment to its left, one pair per bounce, and adding 2 pairs at the right end; it is exact iff every segment to its right is even.

Open: 668 moves (end rules, full sweeps, 3 merges) and the macro level. It has 2-13 separators, recurring tail motifs and left digits growing at power-of-3 rates per pair, so it looks hierarchical. Siblings 188/450/564 (starts D/B/E) show the same coverage, as near-twin orbits that never merge.

template.diff: 6 cells differ from #11b (= #11's table renamed); architecture differs
template.note: Kill #11's .v: shifts S1-S6, windows T1-T14, K(ds; a, b) over d0/d1 digits, carry M, drop, overflow O, one INV. Reusable: the list-of-digits K-config and the list-sweep induction lemmas. Not reusable: our carry is a parity transducer that changes digit lengths, plus a separate eat phase E and a multi-level macro, so the rules and the invariant are new.

strategy: Rule the 5 unruled event families (0.7% of record moves) to get an exact abstract list machine for all four starts. Then find the macro hierarchy and an invariant that keeps 11 from sitting directly left of 00 when a leftward sweep crosses it. The formal side can reuse #11's list-sweep lemmas.
risks: The macro level is a hierarchical counter with no template (like the parked R4/#32), so an invariant may be out of reach.
Every branch is decided by parities of large transferred numbers. A pseudo-random parity sequence would make it cryptid-like (no sign of this so far).
668 record moves to 1e10 have no validated rule yet, and the observed parity law fails at 17 of 60 eat starts.
